messages:
maria (support): Hi team — Acme (tenant acme_inc) just flagged a behavior regression after last rollout. They send the same prompt twice and sometimes get a short factual answer, other times a hallucinated paragraph. They pasted two responses, same prompt and headers. :worried:

lee (customer): here are the two responses and the request id headers we captured:
Request: POST /v1/generate model=rwd-30b, tenant=acme_inc
request-id: req_8a2f9c

Response A (short): 
{
  "text": "The enzyme X is primarily produced in the liver and functions to..."
}

Response B (long/hallucination):
{
  "text": "In ancient trials the enzyme X was codified by the 12th-century monks... [fictional history]"
}

maria (support): Both requests came within 2s of each other from their prod app. They see this ~8% of the time, started after the model/infra rollout yesterday at ~10:20 UTC. They pinned traffic to rwd-30b earlier but we are seeing fallbacks in logs to rwd-30b-quant and rwd-legacy-16k.

jon (sre): I pulled routing traces for req_8a2f9c and another nearby id req_8a2f9f. Traces show different backend variants selected by the smart-router: one routed to pool:rwd-30b-std-us-east, the other to pool:rwd-30b-quant-eu-west (fallback due to capacity). Fallback policy in the rollout config allows cross-variant routing.

sam (eng-runtime): :eyes: That would explain semantic drift — quantized variant still served but we expected deterministic postprocessing normalization. Did we enable the new variant mixing flag in rollout? config: 
```
rollout: rwd-30b:v12
routing_policy:
  prefer: rwd-30b-std
  fallback: [rwd-30b-quant, rwd-legacy]
  allow_variant_mix: true
```

sam (eng-runtime): If allow_variant_mix is true, identical requests can land on different kernels; we rely on output-normalization to match behavior but that wasn't applied to rwd-30b-quant during the deploy (missed a postprocess hook).

jon (sre): Metrics support this: fallback-rate for acme_inc spiked from 1%->10% at 10:22 UTC, latency for quant variant is slightly lower but perplexing diffs in token logits observed.

maria (support): Customer asks for an immediate mitigation — they want consistency. What are options?

sam (eng-runtime): Short term: pin their tenant to a single variant via tenant config to avoid mixing. Command for tenant config API:
```
PATCH /v1/tenants/acme_inc
{ "routing": { "variant_preference": ["rwd-30b-std"] } }
```
This forces deterministic routing. Medium term: revert allow_variant_mix or enable normalization hook on rwd-30b-quant.

jon (sre): I'll roll a targeted policy change to disable allow_variant_mix for the rwd-30b rollout at the cluster-level for impacted tenants, and notify infra.

maria (support): Lee, can you confirm if pinning is acceptable for Acme? They said they need consistency for their billing-critical flows.

lee (customer): Pinning temporarily is fine. We need a permanent fix though — our users noticed wrong legal statements in the hallucinated output. This is high priority.

sam (eng-runtime): Agreed. Action items:
- sam: enable missing postprocess normalization on rwd-30b-quant and run validation against canonical prompt set (ETA 4h)
- jon: disable allow_variant_mix for rwd-30b rollout for acme_inc and affected customers (ETA 30m)
- maria: apply tenant pin for acme_inc and communicate rollback steps to customer (ETA 15m)
- run regression job across 500 seed prompts to validate parity (blocker until pass rate > 99%)

incidents-bot: incident created INC-2026-432, priority=P1, owner=@sam (eng-runtime)

maria (support): Thanks — I'll send the patch commands and status updates to Acme. Keeping thread here for internal updates.

jon (sre): Note for postmortem: routing telemetry should include variant_label and postprocess_version in trace to make this faster next time.

sam (eng-runtime): Logging that. I'll post a summary once normalization is back and regression job finishes.

lee (customer): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Will monitor and report any anomalies. :thumbsup:
